decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed increased its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Output appeared poised to continue growing at a good pace before the tragic toll of Hurricane Katrina.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that economic growth was solid until Hurricane Katrina caused widespread disruption.

changes.quote: Higher energy and other costs have the potential to add to inflation pressures.
changes.explanation: The Fed added that rising energy costs might create upward pressure on inflation.

changes.quote: However, core inflation has been relatively low in recent months and longer-term inflation expectations remain contained.
changes.explanation: The Fed adjusted its assessment to note that core inflation has remained relatively low recently.

changes.quote: Voting against was Mark W. Olson, who preferred no change in the federal funds rate target at this meeting.
changes.explanation: One committee member dissented, preferring to leave the interest rate target unchanged.

tone_quotes.quote: Higher energy and other costs have the potential to add to inflation pressures.
With underlying inflation expected to be contained, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.77% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.26% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.71% would rise by about $1.90 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 271k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.6% over the past year (August 2005); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +7 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to continue removing monetary policy accommodation at a measured pace. At the same time, it indicates that policymakers will respond to changes in economic prospects as needed.
